official_measurement_examples.name: Regulation 7 core duty
official_measurement_examples.fact: Regulation 7 requires appropriate and properly prepared materials to be correctly used or fixed and building work to be carried out in a workmanlike manner.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2013 Approved Document 7 date
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance records the 2013 Approved Document 7 taking effect on 1 July 2013 alongside construction-products changes.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2018 additional requirements
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2018 amendment introduced additional Regulation 7 requirements for materials in external walls and specified attachments of defined relevant buildings.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2018 classification test
official_measurement_examples.fact: For the in-scope 2018 ban, government guidance identifies A1 or A2-s1,d0 classifications subject to statutory exemptions and scope.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2022 scope update
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government's combustible-materials review page was updated in 2022 to reflect extension of the regulatory scope; the date and building scope must be checked before applying the rule.

official_measurement_examples.name: Product versus use
official_measurement_examples.fact: A construction product being lawfully placed on the market does not by itself prove that its selection and installation satisfy Regulation 7 for a particular building.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 reform status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2026 Construction Products Reform White Paper describes proposed reforms and review work; it is not itself a replacement for current Regulation 7 requirements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Regulation 7 materials and workmanship compliance does not grant planning permission or establish parcel development capacity.

core_rules: Regulation 7 compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not Regulation 7 compliance
product market compliance is not proof of correct product selection for a building
correct product selection is not proof of correct installation
2018 combustible-material restrictions apply only within their statutory scope
A1 or A2-s1,d0 classification must not be generalized beyond the applicable requirement
exempt material category must be evidenced
historic material rule must retain its effective date
2026 reform White Paper is not current replacement legislation
consultation proposal is not adopted guidance
impact assessment is not project approval
materials compliance does not create ownership or access rights
no parcel materials clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
